name: Qualcomm OnQ blog: 'Qualcomm AI200 Accelerator for Generative AI' (Feb 2023)
notes: Qualcomm's own OnQ engineering blog introducing AI200, read via browser on 2026-10-03 (qualcomm.com serves almost nothing to web_extract - it gates on a Qualcomm ID - so the browser is required). Qualifies as a vendor primary source for the AI200's positioning but NOT for a spec table: it gives no TOPS figure, no memory capacity, no bus width and no TDP. Its substantive content is architectural and commercial: AI200 is described as supporting generative AI and LLMs at the data centre edge with a cloud-inference pricing model, and as building on the Hexagon AI/AI Engine lineage. Because it publishes no throughput number, it cannot be used to fill a flops row - which is exactly why the AI200 record's compute field stays null rather than being back-computed from the AI100's TOPS figure. NOTE the naming continuity trap: the chip is 'Qualcomm AI200' while the inference card is sold as the 'Qualcomm Cloud AI 100' family - Qualcomm kept the Cloud AI 100 card name for the AI200-based card, so 'Cloud AI 100 Ultra' and 'AI200' can refer to the same product generation and the repo should not treat them as two unrelated parts. | DEAD-LINK VERIFIED 2026-10-04. THREE independent GET probes return HTTP 404 (7.6KB body, empty <title>, no AI200 content) - Qualcomm's news CMS has retired the post. The existing note already establishes the important limit: this blog gives positioning, not a spec table (no TOPS, no memory, no bus width, no TDP), so its loss costs no number. The substantive architectural and commercial claims survive only in this record and in the Wayback Machine; archiving was not done, so archived_url correctly stays null.
